correctness.rationale: Adding and subtracting the two log-swap equations gives (1−a)(X−Y)=2z and (1+a)(X+Y)=2ρ, where z=log(X/Y)>0. The ratio (X−Y)/(X+Y)=tanh(z/2) yields ρ=(1+a)C(z)/(1−a), whose strict increase from 2(1+a)/(1−a) establishes exactly the existence and uniqueness domain. At the first phase, the symmetry-reduced Jacobian P·DF has trace −aS and determinant −D, with S=X+Y and D=1−S+(1−a²)XY. The two-step derivative is its square. The quadratic Schur conditions reduce to 1+D>0 and 1−aS−D>0; the third follows as aS>0. Since S/(XY)=(1−a)sinh(z)/z and J=Cz/sinh(z), the inequalities become exactly a<A(z) and C−(1+a)J<1−a. A and C increase strictly while J decreases, giving unique boundaries. At z₋ the latter left side is aC, so the window closes only where A=1/(1+C), an intersection of strictly opposed curves. At the lower endpoint the reduced root is −1 with the other in (−1,1); at the upper endpoint D=−1 and 0<aS<2 for each nonempty window, so the reduced roots are conjugate unit-modulus with nonzero real part and their squares are also a conjugate pair. At collision the reduced polynomial is (λ+1)². A bounded independent numeric evaluation using the equivalent collision equation cosh(z)−1=C(z) gives z≈1.953977972619354 and a≈0.277839040264087. The frozen witness satisfies the exact swap equations, and the positive-term log(4) series with its geometric tail bound validates its two strict Schur inequalities.
residual_risks: The proof is local and exponential, not a statement about nonlinear boundary dynamics, global basins, or other two-cycle types. Numerical evaluations are corroboration only.
